chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah sends down aid (provision) from the sky to the servant in proportion to the expenditure. So whoever is certain of the Replacement (Allah's return), his soul will be generous with spending.

key_terms.النَّفَقَة: Spending, typically on family or in charity
key_terms.الْخَلَف: The Replacement (Allah providing what was spent)
key_terms.الْمَعُونَة: Divine aid or provision sent from heaven

ai.seo_question: How does spending money affect divine provision according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the reciprocal relationship between human generosity and divine sustenance, emphasizing that Allah's provision is dispensed according to the measure of one's spending. It highlights the psychological and spiritual prerequisite of 'yaqin' (certainty) in Allah's promise of replacement, which overcomes stinginess and fosters voluntary charity. This concept aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of 'kaff' (substitution) as a divine guarantee for those who spend in His cause.
